Reference: Coursebook - IIT Foundation Chemistry Class 9; Chapter - Atomic Structure; Page number - 2.1–2.14

Assessment Test I Time: 30 min.
Directions for questions from 1 to 15: Select the correct answer from the given options.

1. Which of the following is the correct electronic configuration of an element
with atomic number 29?
(a) 2, 8, 18, 1 (b) 2, 8, 17, 2 (c) 2, 9, 16, 2 (d) 2, 18, 9

2. Identify the element from the given configuration.
$a, 4a, (6a + 1)$, and $(a - 1)$
(a) Scandium (b) Chromium
(c) Iron (d) Manganese

3. Which of the following postulates of Dalton’s atomic theory was proved
wrong with the discovery of radioactivity?
(a) Matter is constituted of the tiniest particles called atoms.
(b) Atoms are indivisible.
(c) Atoms of same elements are identical in all aspects.
(d) Atoms of different elements are different in all aspects.

4. The ratio of atomic numbers of two elements 'X' and 'Y' is 1:7. The radius of
the third orbit of single electron species of X is 1.587 $\text{\AA}$. Identify the penulti-
mate shell of Y.

(a) N-shell (b) M-shell
(c) L-shell (d) O-shell

5. A dipositive ion of element 'A' is isoelectronic with inert gas 'X'. X possesses
three completely filled shells. The number of electrons present in the ante-
penultimate shell of atom of element A is ______.
(a) 18 (b) 8
(c) 32 (d) 2

6. According to Rutherford’s atomic model, __________.
(a) protons are the lightest positively charged particles
(b) electrons rotate in the opposite spin to the rotation of protons
(c) electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain fixed paths
(d) electrons revolve around the nucleus with high velocity
